---
# No title:/author: — the letterhead pulled in below IS the heading, and it
# must be identical to the cover letter's.
#
# Body font: 12pt in .docx (Word's default), 11pt in .pdf. Both sit inside
# the required 10-12pt range. Section headings come out larger than body
# text in both formats, which is the intended contrast.
format:
  docx:
    number-sections: false
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    geometry: margin=0.75in
    fontsize: 11pt
    linestretch: 1
    indent: false
    colorlinks: false
    number-sections: false
---

<!-- ######################################################################
RULES THAT APPLY TO EVERY SECTION BELOW — read once, then fill in.

ORDER is fixed by the chronological-resume structure the instructor
specified: identifying info, education, employment, skills, activities.
Reverse chronological WITHIN each section (most recent entry first).

NO FIRST-PERSON PRONOUNS anywhere. No "I," "me," "my," "us." Bullets start
with a verb, not a subject.

PARALLEL STRUCTURE. Within one entry, every bullet takes the same
grammatical shape. Past roles use past tense throughout; your current role
uses present tense throughout. Do not mix.

ACTION VERBS, NOT REPEATED. Each bullet opens with a different strong verb.
Verbs that fit this BD role: Analyzed, Researched, Sourced, Qualified,
Built, Negotiated, Coordinated, Presented, Delivered, Streamlined,
Increased, Secured, Forecasted, Mapped. Do not open three bullets with
"Managed."

TAILORING. This resume is aimed at the 2311 Climate Solutions Business
Development Intern ad. Pull its language in where it is HONESTLY true of
your experience: market research, commercialization strategy, pipeline
management, lead qualification, partnerships, market intelligence,
cross-functional collaboration, industry trends.

PUNCTUATION CONSISTENCY. Pick one rule for bullet endings — periods on all
of them, or periods on none — and hold it across the whole document.

ONE PAGE. If it spills onto page two, cut bullets rather than shrinking the
font below 10pt or narrowing the margins further. Check there is no empty
trailing page before submitting.

NO REFERENCES SECTION, and no "References available upon request."
###################################################################### -->

## Education

***

<!-- Reverse chronological. Include the actual degree abbreviation (B.A.,
B.S., B.B.A.), major, school, city, state, and graduation year. Mark an
in-progress degree as "Expected [Month Year]" — do not imply it is finished.

GPA is optional. Include it only if it helps you; if you list it, list it
for every entry that has one. High school belongs here only if it is
directly relevant to this position, which for most college students it is
not — delete that entry.

Relevant coursework is useful when work experience is thin. Choose courses
this employer would care about: market research, finance, statistics,
economics, business communication. -->

**B.S., [Mechanical Engineering]**\
[Texas Tech] — [Lubbock, Texas]\
*Expected [May 2028]*

- Relevant coursework: [course; course; course]
- [GPA: 0.00 — delete this bullet if you are not listing GPA]

## Experience

***

<!-- Reverse chronological. Every entry needs: job title, organization,
city, state, and dates of employment. Two to three bullets minimum per
entry, each demonstrating a skill, experience, or ability.

Write bullets in STAR shape and land the RESULT. "Researched 40 prospective
accounts and built a qualified pipeline that produced 6 first meetings"
beats "Responsible for market research." Quantify wherever the number is
real — counts, percentages, dollar figures, timeframes.

Volunteer work counts and goes in this same section. Unrelated jobs still
earn a spot if you can connect them to transferable skills this ad names.

Copy the block below for each additional entry. Keep the formatting
identical across entries — that consistency is the graded alignment. -->

**[Job Title]**\
[Organization] — [City, State]\
*[Month Year] – [Month Year]*

- [Action verb + what you did + measurable result.]
- [Different action verb + what you did + measurable result.]
- [Different action verb + what you did + measurable result.]

**[Job Title]**\
[Organization] — [City, State]\
*[Month Year] – [Month Year]*

- [Action verb + what you did + measurable result.]
- [Different action verb + what you did + measurable result.]

## Skills

***

<!-- HARD, VERIFIABLE SKILLS ONLY. The instructor explicitly warns against
subjective self-assessments — do not list Time Management, Leadership,
Hard-working, Detail-oriented, Team Player, or Creative. Those are your
opinion of yourself; your bullets above are supposed to demonstrate them.

Avoid redundancy: if you name the specific tools, do not also claim to be
"skilled in software."

This ad explicitly requires Microsoft Office proficiency for analysis and
presentations, so name the actual applications.

Languages: only fluent or conversational ones. Your native language does
not need to be listed. Delete the line if it does not apply. -->

- **[Category, e.g. Analysis]:** [tool; tool; tool]
- **[Category, e.g. Research]:** [tool; tool; tool]
- **Languages:** [Language (fluent); Language (conversational)]
